heroHeadline: UN Global Forest Goals Report: 40M Hectares Lost in a Decade; Amazon at 11-Year Low But Degradation Surges
heroSubtitle: The UN's Global Forest Goals Report 2026 (released May 11) confirmed global forest area fell more than 40 million hectares between 2015 and 2025, with financing still less than half of the $571 billion per year needed. Separately, Brazil's Amazon deforestation hit its lowest rate in 11 years (~5,796 km²/yr, down 73% from 2021 peak) — but a May 8 Washington Post investigation warned that forest degradation from logging, drought, and El Niño wildfires now affects an estimated 40% of the remaining Amazon, a threat largely invisible in official metrics. A new tipping-point study found deforestation of 22–28% combined with 1.5–1.9°C of warming could trigger irreversible Amazon savannification by the 2040s.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNEP, FAO, UNCCD, IUCN, WRI Global Forest Watch, INPE, and Tier 2 science outlets. Pledge figures reflect commitments; verified restoration is substantially lower.
